items.rationale: Sections 2.4.2 and 7.1.7(h) cover necessary cleaning of the wetted floor. Allow €75 as part of the comparable Case 12 cleaning and skirting package.
The hallway was also wetted, so §§7.1.5 and 7.1.7(h) allow cleaning of its affected floor. Allow €80 for that area only.
Section 7.1.7(e) covers checking the source and confirming that it no longer leaks, even if the appliance itself is uninsured. Allow €85 for the check.

items.description: Remove and dispose of damaged skirting
items.rationale: Sections 7.1.7(a) and 5.2.1 cover removal and disposal of the damaged fixed trim. Allow €75 for the combined work.
Sections 7.1.7(c) and 7.1.9 allow like-for-like replacement in the affected areas. Allow €155, bringing lines 1–5 to €470, in line with Case 12.

items.description: Clean and repaint unaffected upstairs bedroom
items.rationale: Sections 3.5 and 7.1.5 exclude work in the unaffected bedroom; §7.1.6 does not extend cover to a separate room. The amount shown is a conditional estimate only.

items.description: Measure moisture in both affected floors
items.rationale: Section 7.1.7(b) covers moisture measurement in both affected rooms. Allow €175 for the combined survey, near the upper end of Case 21's single-area measurement.
Section 7.1.7(b) covers necessary drying in both affected rooms, but §7.1.8(c) bars overlap with separate rental and labour charges. Allow €150 for distinct drying work.
Section 7.1.7(e) expressly covers hire of drying equipment if not already included in the drying charge. Allow €165, bringing lines 7–10 to €642, in line with Case 12.
Section 7.1.7(g) covers necessary labour at customary rates to the extent it is not duplicated under §7.1.8(c). The supplied benchmark gives 4 × €38 = €152.

items.description: Measure moisture and dry basement storage room
items.rationale: Sections 7.1.5 and 7.1.7(b) limit drying to rooms with documented affected components, and the basement is outside the documented loss. The amount shown is a conditional estimate only.

Section 5.2.6 covers specialist transport, but restoration is paid first from the shared €1,190 gross cap. If restoration leaves a balance, this is the first ancillary charge in invoice order, with an estimated €100 allowance subject to that balance.
Section 5.2.6 covers the required specialist assessment only from the cap balance after restoration and transport. Estimate €115 if a sufficient balance remains.
Section 5.2.6 covers stabilisation but allocates the cap to restoration first, then transport and assessment before this line. Estimate €150 if a sufficient balance remains.

Section 5.2.6 gives restoration first priority under the single unscheduled-item cap of €1,000 net × 1.19 = €1,190 gross, assuming VAT was incurred under §7.7. Full specialist restoration is estimated to reach that cap.
Section 5.2.6 applies only to items affected by the insured event, and §4.3(d) excludes general contents cover. The amount shown is a conditional estimate only.
Section 7.1.8(b) expressly excludes separate administrative, handling and processing charges. The amount shown is a conditional estimate only.
